title: ActionsPanel: add 'Actions – Button' mode for on() handler authoring on button instances
description:
When the user selects a button instance on stage and opens the Actions panel (F9), they should see 'Actions – Button' mode with an event list sidebar (press, release, releaseOutside, rollOver, rollOut, dragOver, dragOut) and a per-event script editor — exactly like the 'Actions – Movie Clip' mode does for onClipEvent handlers on MovieClip instances.

Current state:
- ActionsPanel supports two modes: frame-script mode (default) and 'Actions – Movie Clip' mode (when selectedMovieClipInstance + onClipActionsChange are provided, Shell.tsx ~line 1369).
- Shell.tsx computes selectedMovieClipInstance only for items with symbolType === 'movieclip' (line 1377). No equivalent exists for button instances.
- buttonActions lives on Symbol (packages/core/src/model/types.ts line 226), not on the instance. This is correct: in Flash 8, on() handlers are part of the button definition.

Implementation:
1. In Shell.tsx, add a selectedButtonInstance useMemo that returns the resolved Symbol (symbolType === 'button') when a button SymbolInstance is selected, similar to selectedMovieClipInstance.
2. Add a handleButtonActionsChange callback that calls pushDoc to update the Symbol's buttonActions array in doc.library.items.
3. Add a 'button' mode to ActionsPanel: new prop 'selectedButtonSymbol?: Symbol' + 'onButtonActionsChange?'. When set, render a sidebar with on() event types and a per-event script editor using the same ScriptEditor component. The event list should show: press, release, releaseOutside, rollOver, rollOut, dragOver, dragOut.
4. Wire the new props through Shell.tsx's <ActionsPanel> invocation (line ~3861).
5. Verify that button on() scripts authored here round-trip through FLA save/load (already supported via Symbol.buttonActions in the FLA serializer) and appear in the published SWF as BUTTONCONDACTION records (already handled by packages/swf/src/buttons.ts line 336).

Acceptance: author a button with on(press){ gotoAndStop(2); } via the Actions panel, publish, click the button in Ruffle, confirm the stage changes frame.
